Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of needs (from our conversation):
- Latency targets: P50 ~30–50ms, P95 <= 250ms, P99 target to define per-route for risk-sensitive flows.
- Throughput: ~8k requests/minute peak for account lookup endpoints, sustained ~2k/minute.
- Concurrency: spikes up to 150 concurrent streaming sessions during batch runs.
- Streaming: server-side streaming required for real-time UX in the dashboard (chunked tokens).
- Multi-region: must serve US and EU customers from local regions; APAC is a lower-latency preference for growth.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU; APAC customers prefer APAC residency where possible.

Proposed next steps:
1) Could you confirm the P99 target you need for the two highest-risk routes (auth & transaction-history)?
2) Any hard constraints on cross-region replication for user-identifying telemetry (we discussed audit logs possibly staying in region)?
3) I’ll loop in Aditya (SE) to provide a short SLO/throughput estimate and an attachment with configuration options (batching, cache TTLs, recommended instance types).

If that looks right, can we aim to get the P99s and any residency blacklines by EOD Wed so we can include them in the draft mutual action plan?

Hi Nikhil —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) P99 targets: for auth endpoints we need P99 <= 400ms (these are lightweight calls but high QPS). For transaction-history (which can return larger payloads) we want P99 <= 800ms. If streaming is used we care more about first-byte latency for UX (first token delivered under 200ms).

2) Throughput/Concurrency: the numbers you have match our estimates. To be conservative, assume a 20% growth buffer for Q3–Q4.

3) Data residency: EU data must remain in EU at rest and in transit; for analytics/audit logs we can accept pseudonymized summaries leaving region but raw audit logs must be stored in EU. For APAC, we prefer APAC residency but it’s not a blocker for initial rollout — latency matters more.

4) Compliance evidence: Can you provide a short note on where logs/audit trails are stored and retention controls? Procurement will need this for the vendor questionnaire.

If you can send the SLO estimate and a snippet on audit/log residency, we’ll share internally and aim to get back with any procurement redlines by Friday.

Hi Samir —

Thanks — I put together a short technical reply and attached an SLO estimate spreadsheet (redwood-slo-estimates.xlsx). High-level answers below: 

SLO/Latency guidance (estimates are for Redwood Dedicated with autoscale + regional routing):
- Auth endpoints (small payloads, low compute): P50 ~20–35ms, P95 ~120–180ms, P99 ~300–450ms depending on burst concurrency. To hit P99 <= 400ms consistently we recommend a dedicated pool with 2x baseline capacity for auth routing and aggressive KV prefix caching (TTL 30s) to eliminate repeated work.
- Transaction-history (larger payloads): P50 ~60–120ms, P95 ~300–500ms, P99 ~600–850ms. For these routes we recommend response streaming with chunked payloads to keep first-byte latency low and to allow progressive rendering.
- Streaming first-byte: With server-side streaming enabled and a small initial generation window we can get first-byte under 150–200ms for most requests, even under load, provided the region has local capacity.

Throughput & concurrency guidance:
- Peak 8k RPM: Redwood Dedicated with 4 medium GPU workers per region (NVIDIA A10/A30 class equivalent) with autoscale headroom covers this comfortably with continuous batching. See spreadsheet for token-level cost estimates.
- Concurrency spikes (150 streaming sessions): use sticky sessions routed to regional pools, streaming connections are long-lived so we recommend increasing keep-alive and configuring a burst pool to absorb spikes (we typically reserve ~15% capacity for burst).

Regional routing & data residency:
- Routing: requests are routed by policy (geo from request + customer tag). We can pin customers/accounts to a region and fallback to nearest region if local capacity is exhausted.
- EU residency: raw logs and audit trails can be retained in EU S3 buckets (or customer-managed object store) with KMS keys scoped to the EU. We support per-account retention policies and automatic pseudonymization pipelines for analytics exports.
- Cross-region replication: we avoid replicating raw audit logs; aggregated metrics can be replicated to US for platform analytics once pseudonymized.

Operational suggestions:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for auth flows (TTL 15–30s) to reduce tail latency.
- Use streaming for large-payload endpoints and measure first-byte separately in SLOs.
- Canary the EU routing policy with a small % of traffic to validate latency and failover behavior before full cutover.

Attached: redwood-slo-estimates.xlsx (contains per-route latency estimates, instance sizing, token cost estimates, and recommended autoscale policies)

Happy to hop on a short technical call this week to walk the spreadsheet and proposed canary plan.
